text.p: Turkmenistan's consumer price inflation is likely to fall this year to 45-50 percent from over 500 percent last year, a central bank official said on Tuesday.

"Over the last two years the Central Bank has managed to stamp out hyperinflation, which soared to 1,362 percent in 1995 and fell to 545.8 percent in 1996," said Sergei Bogomolov, head of the Central Bank of Turkmenistan's financial policy and research department.

Bogomolov told Reuters the moderate inflation target for this year was backed by the central bank's tight credit and monetary policies. Monthly inflation in May was 2.6 percent, almost unchanged from April's 2.5 percent.
He said prices in the first five months of this year grew by 17.2 percent, much slower than expected initially.
"Starting this year, the central bank has practically stopped financing the state budget, and is financing commercial banks only through auctions of its credit funds," he said.
Bogomolov said low and controllable inflation would lead to further cuts in the central bank's refinancing rate, which has fallen to 47 percent from 105 percent in January this year.
"This will become a signal for commercial banks to steadily lower interest on both credits and deposits," he said.
